analysis:
This batch contains only documentation and changelog changes: changelog.d/ssd-restore-without-eval-lock.md (head 1-9) and docs/architecture/inference.md (hunk @@ -249,6 +249,14 @@). They describe a behavior change: complete-checkpoint SSD restore now creates destinations from host bytes off the engine queue, without evaluating or fencing them under MLX's process-wide evalLock, so staging no longer waits behind another request's prefill chunk. The actual implementation (CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift, SSDPrefixCache staging/completeStaging/endAdoption) is not in this batch, so this is a coverage limit.

The next pass should check:
- T-041 (SSD tier, A-001): whether skipping eval/fence still preserves DBK3 AES-GCM authentication before restored bytes are adopted, cacheSalt scope checks, and staging-reservation release paths.
- T-028: residual buffers.
- Data races: unfenced destinations read by the engine while the host is still copying into them.
- SEC-035 TTFT oracle: faster restore under contention (2.6-3.8 s down to about 0.35 s) widens the hit/miss timing gap. That gap is already an accepted risk, unchanged in kind and same-account only.
- GlobalKVCacheBudget accounting for host-created destinations.

The docs make no security-control claims beyond referencing ssd-kv-cache.md#complete-checkpoint-payload. No finding is supported from docs alone.
